speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. To determine the cause, can you tell me how many days old your baby is and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Malrotation with Volvulus.

I am concerned because the baby is only six hours old and has bilious vomiting, which is a surgical emergency. While the family history of pyloric stenosis is noted, it typically presents at 3-6 weeks of age, not immediately after birth. I need to confirm this immediately with an X-ray and ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Xray; REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
